why: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but the risk has shifted to politics: after the Democratic sweep, UBS says ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses, and Microsoft is reportedly tightening oversight of neocloud projects. Spending is still debt-funded, with free cash flow negative at three of the four biggest spenders. New on Tue: momentum for a US plan to block imports of Chinese data-centre equipment, which Amazon, Alphabet and Meta oppose.

Nvidia fell about 3% on Thursday to around US$146, a fresh low since mid-2025, after falling 2.9% on Wednesday despite beating forecasts (Q3 revenue US$115.8bn, +103%). AMD fell about 8% after short seller Hunterbrook alleged its firmware reached a blacklisted Chinese server maker (AMD denies wrongdoing). Broadcom and Micron fell about 2%. The board won’t bring back Jensen Huang, and the WSJ reports an SEC disclosure probe. Good numbers no longer lifting the stock is a classic late-cycle sign.

A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is about 95% priced, with 69% odds of 50 bp of hikes by end-January. The October minutes showed almost all officials expect further hikes. Slightly higher jobless claims and a weaker Philadelphia factory survey on Thursday have not shifted the pricing yet.

Oracle about −3% and CoreWeave about −5% on Thursday; CoreWeave jumped 10% early with Anthropic’s debut, then reversed. Oracle is about 40% down in 2026 with ~US$108bn of debt and a bondholder lawsuit; its default protection is reported near 300 bp. CoreWeave is pricing a term loan at a 7–7.5% yield. ETFs that would bet against CoreWeave, Oracle and Meta debt have been filed with the SEC. No newer CoreWeave level since 1,268 bp (5 Nov).

Anthropic opened on Nasdaq at US$111.50, 34% above its US$83 IPO price, then faded to close at US$97.17 (+17%) after raising a record ~US$81bn. Retail investors sold other tech, especially AMD, to buy it, so the debut drained the wider AI trade rather than reviving it. Nvidia reportedly cut a proposed OpenAI data-centre guarantee from US$250bn to ~US$105bn. (Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic.)
Eased 2 bp to 5.05% on Thursday as stocks fell 2%: a mild flight-to-safety signal, not the sharp fall that marks a panic. Yields are still near their highest since 2002.

WTI rose 0.9% to US$83.08 and Brent to about US$92 on Thursday as reports of mines in the Strait of Hormuz offset a US stockpile build. Oil is no longer falling, so it is not easing the inflation pressure behind Fed hikes.
High-yield spread 323 bp on 13 Nov (320 bp on 12 Nov): broad credit is still calm. IMF: US bank loans to non-bank lenders rose 18% in 2026.

Thursday was broad selling: more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell, the S&P 500 lost 2.0% (sixth straight loss), the Nasdaq 2.3%, the Dow 2.2% and small caps 1.8%. Gold fell 2.1% to a fresh one-year low, so havens are falling with shares.
